fullPassage:
Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because of the abundance and diversity of life they support. Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, coral reefs provide shelter for about one quarter of all known marine species. They also serve as natural barriers that protect coastal communities from powerful waves and storms. Furthermore, coral reefs are sometimes referred to as the medicine chests of the sea because many organisms found in coral reefs are used in medicines. Over 500 million people around the world rely on coral reefs for food, income, and coastal protection.

Unfortunately, coral reefs around the world are in serious danger. Scientists estimate that about half of the Great Barrier Reef has disappeared over the past few decades. If current trends continue, most coral reefs could be gone by 2050. Several factors contribute to this decline. Destructive fishing practices, the overpopulation of natural predators such as the crown-of-thorns starfish, and careless tourism all damage coral reefs. However, the leading cause of coral reef destruction is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. Corals thrive in water temperatures between 20 and 28 degrees Celsius, but when the temperature rises above 30 degrees, they begin to die. Plastic waste that enters the ocean also poses a significant threat, as it can smother corals and block the sunlight they need to survive.

Fortunately, scientists and engineers around the world are developing innovative technologies to help save coral reefs. In Florida, researchers have designed a jellyfish-like robot that can gently swim around coral reefs to monitor their health without disturbing the delicate ecosystem. In Australia, an underwater robot has been created to eliminate the crown-of-thorns starfish, which destroy large areas of coral. The robot identifies the starfish and gives them a toxic salt injection. In Hong Kong, scientists are using 3D printing technology to create artificial coral structures that provide support for new coral growth.

There are also many things that ordinary people can do to help protect coral reefs. First, we should avoid using beauty products that contain microplastics, as these tiny particles end up in the ocean and harm marine life. Second, when swimming in the ocean, we should choose reef-safe sunscreen that does not contain chemicals harmful to corals. Third, we can volunteer for beach cleanup activities to prevent trash from entering the ocean. Finally, we can spread awareness about the importance of coral reefs by sharing information with friends and family.

Marine Gardening Day is celebrated on May 10th every year in Korea. Korea was the first country in the world to designate a national day for marine ecosystem conservation. On this day, people participate in activities to restore and protect sea forests, which are vital habitats for marine creatures.

questions.passage: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because of the abundance and diversity of life they support. Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, coral reefs provide shelter for about one quarter of all known marine species. They also serve as natural barriers __________ protect coastal communities from powerful waves and storms.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 natural barriers(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. "폭풍으로부터 해안 공동체를 보호하는 자연적 방벽"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ that: 사물 선행사(natural barriers) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ② who: 사람 선행사용 → barriers는 사물
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나 protect의 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + that/which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: Plastic waste that enters the ocean also poses a significant threat, as it can smother corals and block the sunlight they need to survive. Destructive fishing practices and the overpopulation of natural predators damage coral reefs, __________ their recovery.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 현재분사 blocking이 적절하다. "산호초를 훼손하여, 그 결과 회복을 막는다"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ blocking: 결과를 나타내는 분사구문 (현재분사)
❌ ① block: 원형 → 접속사 없이 연결 불가
❌ ② blocked: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ④ to block: to부정사 → 결과 분사구문에 부적절
det.tip: 결과 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → "그 결과 ~하다"

questions.passage: Furthermore, coral reefs are sometimes referred to as the medicine chests of the sea because many organisms __________ in coral reefs are used in medicines. Over 500 million people around the world rely on coral reefs for food, income, and coastal protection.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: organisms(유기체)가 산호초에서 발견되는 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 found가 적절하다. "산호초에서 발견되는 많은 유기체들"
det.analysis:
✅ ① found: 과거분사 → organisms와 수동 관계 (발견되는)
❌ ② finding: 현재분사 → 능동(발견하는)이 되어 부적절
❌ ③ to find: to부정사 → 문법적 부적절
❌ ④ find: 동사원형 → 사용 불가
det.tip: 과거분사의 수식: 명사 + p.p. → 수동 관계 (명사가 동작을 당하는 경우)

questions.passage: Scientists estimate that about half of the Great Barrier Reef has disappeared over the past few decades. If current trends continue, most coral reefs __________ by 2050.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "현재 추세가 계속된다면(If + 현재형)" 미래에 대한 예측이므로 could be gone이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② could be gone: 조건절(If + 현재) + 주절(could + 동사원형) → 미래 가능성
❌ ① are gone: 확정적 표현 → 추정과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ had gone: 과거완료 → 시제 부적절
❌ ④ have gone: 현재완료 → if절과 호응 부적절
❌ ⑤ were going: 과거진행 → 시제 부적절
det.tip: If + 현재형, S + could/may + 동사원형: 미래에 대한 가능성/추정

questions.passage: In Florida, researchers have ①<u>designed</u> a jellyfish-like robot that can gently swim around coral reefs to monitor their health. In Australia, an underwater robot has been ②<u>creating</u> to eliminate the crown-of-thorns starfish. In Hong Kong, scientists are ③<u>using</u> 3D printing technology to create artificial coral structures.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~③ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② creating → created: 로봇이 만들어진 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 created가 적절하다. "has been created" = 현재완료 수동태
det.analysis:
❌ ② creating(능동) → created(수동): 로봇이 스스로 만드는 것이 아니라 만들어진 것
✅ ① designed: have designed → 현재완료 능동 → 올바름
✅ ③ using: are using → 현재진행 → 올바름
det.tip: has/have been + p.p. = 현재완료 수동태: ~되어 왔다

questions.passage: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because of the abundance and diversity of life they support. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "coral reefs provide shelter for about one quarter of all known marine species" → 산호초는 알려진 해양 종의 약 1/4에게 서식지를 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 해양 종의 약 1/4에게 서식지 제공: 본문과 일치
❌ ① "less than one percent"(1% 미만) → 25%가 아님
❌ ③ natural barriers로 보호 → 피해가 아님
❌ ④ "Over 500 million"(5억 명 이상) → 50만 명이 아님
det.tip: 숫자 정보를 정확히 대조: one quarter(1/4), one percent(1%), 500 million(5억)

ch: 산호초는 알려진 해양 종의 약 1/4에게 서식지를 제공한다.
산호초는 해안 공동체에 큰 피해를 준다.

questions.passage: Unfortunately, coral reefs around the world are in serious danger. Scientists estimate that about half of the Great Barrier Reef has disappeared over the past few decades. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "the leading cause of coral reef destruction is the rise in water temperature due to global warming" → 주된 원인은 지구 온난화에 의한 수온 상승이지, 플라스틱 폐기물이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 주된 원인이 플라스틱: 원문에서 leading cause = 수온 상승, 플라스틱은 추가 위협
✅ ① "Destructive fishing practices" → 일치
✅ ② "between 20 and 28 degrees Celsius" → 일치
✅ ④ "above 30 degrees, they begin to die" → 일치
det.tip: leading cause(주된 원인) ≠ a significant threat(심각한 위협) — 주원인과 부수적 원인 구별

ch: 산호초 파괴의 주된 원인은 플라스틱 폐기물이다.
수온이 30도 이상 오르면 산호가 죽기 시작한다.

questions.passage: There are also many things that ordinary people can do to help protect coral reefs. First, we should avoid using beauty products that contain microplastics, as these tiny particles end up in the ocean and harm marine life. Second, when swimming in the ocean, we should choose reef-safe sunscreen that does not contain chemicals harmful to corals. Third, we can volunteer for beach cleanup activities to prevent trash from entering the ocean. Finally, we can spread awareness about the importance of coral reefs by sharing information with friends and family.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산호초의 중요성(P1), 위기(P2), 기술적 해결책(P3), 개인의 실천(P4)을 다루며 산호초의 중요성과 보호 방안을 알리는 것이 목적이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 산호초의 중요성과 보호 방안: 전체 글의 구조(중요성→위기→기술→실천)
❌ ① 아름다움 찬양: 일부 내용일 뿐 전체 목적 아님
❌ ② 상업적 가치: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 경제적 피해 분석: 언급 없음
❌ ⑤ 관광 장려: 오히려 부주의한 관광을 비판
det.tip: 글의 목적: 전체 구조를 파악하여 핵심 주장 도출

ch: 해양 기술의 상업적 가치를 홍보하기 위해
산호초의 중요성과 보호 방안을 알리기 위해
해양 오염의 경제적 피해를 분석하기 위해

questions.passage: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea because of the abundance and diversity of life they support. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산호초가 해안 공동체를 파도와 폭풍으로부터 보호하는 자연 방벽 역할을 하므로, 사람들이 의존하는 것은 해안 보호(coastal protection)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② coastal protection: 앞 문장의 "natural barriers that protect coastal communities"와 일치
❌ ① commercial fishing: 상업 어업은 언급 없음
❌ ③ deep-sea exploration: 심해 탐사는 언급 없음
❌ ④ coral farming: 산호 양식은 언급 없음
det.tip: 빈칸 앞의 "natural barriers" + "protect coastal communities"가 핵심 단서

questions.passage: Unfortunately, coral reefs around the world are in serious danger. Several factors contribute to this decline, including destructive fishing, overpopulation of predators, careless tourism, and rising water temperatures. Fortunately, scientists and engineers around the world are developing __________ to help save coral reefs. In Florida, researchers have designed a jellyfish-like robot for monitoring. In Australia, a robot eliminates harmful starfish. In Hong Kong, 3D printing creates artificial coral structures.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 플로리다의 로봇, 호주의 로봇, 홍콩의 3D 프린팅 등 혁신적 기술(innovative technologies)을 개발하고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② innovative technologies: 로봇, 3D 프린팅 등 첨단 기술 사례들이 뒷받침
❌ ① artificial reproduction: 인공 번식은 구체적 내용과 불일치
❌ ③ traditional methods: 전통적 방법이 아닌 혁신적 기술
❌ ④ government regulations: 정부 규제는 언급 없음
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤의 구체적 사례(로봇, 3D 프린팅)가 상위 개념의 단서

questions.passage: There are also many things that ordinary people can do to help protect coral reefs. First, we should avoid using beauty products that contain microplastics. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 친구와 가족에게 정보를 공유함으로써 산호초의 중요성에 대한 인식을 확산(spread awareness)할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① spread awareness: "by sharing information with friends and family"가 핵심 단서
❌ ② conduct research: 일반인의 실천 사항에 연구는 부적절
❌ ③ build barriers: 방벽 건설은 언급 없음
❌ ④ reduce tourism: 관광 줄이기는 본문 맥락과 불일치
det.tip: "by sharing information"이 수단 → 그 목적은 "인식 확산(spread awareness)"

questions.passage: Coral reefs around the world are in serious danger. Many marine species that depend on coral reefs are now __________ (endanger). Scientists warn that immediate action is needed to prevent further loss.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: endanger(동사) → endangered(형용사): "are + 형용사" 구문에서 해양 종들이 "멸종 위기에 처한" 상태를 나타내는 과거분사형 형용사
det.analysis:
endanger(동사) → endangered(과거분사/형용사)
are ______ : be동사 뒤 보어 → 형용사 필요
endangered species = 멸종 위기 종
det.tip: endanger → endangered / damage → damaged — 동사 → 과거분사형 형용사(상태)

questions.passage: Several factors contribute to the decline of coral reefs. __________ (destroy) fishing practices, the overpopulation of natural predators, and careless tourism all damage coral reefs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: destroy(동사) → destructive(형용사): 명사 fishing practices를 수식하는 형용사가 필요. "파괴적인 어업 관행"
det.analysis:
destroy(동사) → destruction(명사) → destructive(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 fishing practices(명사)를 수식하는 형용사 필요
destructive fishing practices = 파괴적인 어업 관행
det.tip: destroy → destruction → destructive / create → creation → creative — 동사 → 명사 → 형용사

"Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor."

det.korean: "Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor" → 산호초는 해저의 1% 미만을 차지한다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 "less than one percent of the ocean floor"과 진술이 정확히 일치
det.tip: 본문 문장을 그대로 인용한 진술 → True

questions.passage: Unfortunately, coral reefs around the world are in serious danger. Scientists estimate that about half of the Great Barrier Reef has disappeared over the past few decades. If current trends continue, most coral reefs could be gone by 2050. Several factors contribute to this decline. Destructive fishing practices, the overpopulation of natural predators such as the crown-of-thorns starfish, and careless tourism all damage coral reefs. However, the leading cause of coral reef destruction is the rise in water temperature due to global warming. Corals thrive in water temperatures between 20 and 28 degrees Celsius, but when the temperature rises above 30 degrees, they begin to die. Plastic waste that enters the ocean also poses a significant threat, as it can smother corals and block the sunlight they need to survive.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Corals thrive when the water temperature rises above 30 degrees Celsius."

det.korean: 본문: "when the temperature rises above 30 degrees, they begin to die" → 30도 이상에서 죽기 시작한다. "잘 자란다(thrive)"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: thrive(번성) ≠ die(죽다) — 30도 이상에서는 번성이 아닌 사망
det.tip: thrive(번성하다) ↔ die(죽다) — 핵심 동사의 의미 대조

questions.passage: Marine Gardening Day is celebrated on May 10th every year in Korea. Korea was the first country in the world to designate a national day for marine ecosystem conservation. On this day, people participate in activities to restore and protect sea forests, which are vital habitats for marine creatures.
questions.stem:

"Korea was the first country in the world to designate a national day for marine ecosystem conservation."

det.korean: "Korea was the first country in the world to designate a national day for marine ecosystem conservation" → 본문과 정확히 일치 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 원문과 진술이 정확히 일치
det.tip: 본문의 문장을 그대로 인용한 진술 → True

questions.passage: Fortunately, scientists and engineers around the world are developing innovative technologies to help save coral reefs. In Florida, researchers have designed a jellyfish-like robot that can gently swim around coral reefs to monitor their health without disturbing the delicate ecosystem. In Australia, an underwater robot has been created to eliminate the crown-of-thorns starfish, which destroy large areas of coral. The robot identifies the starfish and gives them a toxic salt injection. In Hong Kong, scientists are using 3D printing technology to create artificial coral structures that provide support for new coral growth.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The jellyfish-like robot in Florida eliminates the crown-of-thorns starfish with a toxic injection."

det.korean: 본문에서 불가사리를 제거하는 로봇은 호주(Australia)의 로봇이고, 플로리다의 해파리 모양 로봇은 모니터링(monitor) 용도이다. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: 플로리다 로봇 = 모니터링 / 호주 로봇 = 불가사리 제거 — 장소와 기능이 뒤바뀜
det.tip: 세부 정보(장소-기능 대응)를 정확히 대조: Florida=monitoring, Australia=elimination
